title: Normalized extended-Rees and relative-Spec cone comparison
statement: Let $s:S\hookrightarrow V$ be any closed immersion of schemes. Use its actual extended-Rees zero fibre $s.\ker.\mathrm{normalCone}$ and canonical projection [def-pur-normal-bundle], and its relative-Spec associated-graded cone $C_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I}\mathcal O_V$ with its projection and augmentation section [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. Identify its structural algebra with the pushforward of its structure sheaf by the counit of the affine-morphism/relative-Spec anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec], using the same relative-spectrum construction as [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Define ReesConeNormalized(s,q), for an isomorphism $q:s.\ker.\mathrm{normalCone}\simeq C_s$, to require preservation of the projection and zero section, and the following equality on every affine chart $U\subseteq V$: pullback along its chart map followed by $q$ sends each degree-one ideal class of $a\in\mathcal I(U)$ to $a/t$ modulo $t$ in the extended-Rees quotient. There is a unique such isomorphism: these degree-one identities and the structural map determine all homogeneous degrees. Define reesConeComparison(s) to be this uniquely characterized isomorphism and reesConeComparison_spec its normalization proof. No regularity, Noetherian or smoothness hypothesis is imposed. This supplies the specified Rees-to-relative-Spec transport; the existing section-deformation geometry, cone-to-vector-bundle comparison and bundle adjoints are reused, not defined again.

proof.text: Take a projection- and augmentation-compatible normalized isomorphism supplied by the existence theorem.

For two normalized comparisons, evaluate their degree-one pullbacks on every Rees affine chart. Both equal a/t modulo t. The chart section map is invertible over the corresponding ambient affine open, so their pullbacks agree before chart restriction.
Apply conormalCone_hom_ext with the relative-Spec counit algebra isomorphism; equality of the underlying scheme morphisms gives equality of isomorphisms.

proof_origin.note: Formal uniqueness from degree-one detection, retaining a separately stated normalized existence input.
